messages:
maya: quick ping — opened a small PR updating the quickstart streaming example; noticed a race when we call cancel() right after starting the stream. can someone eyeball? https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4823 :pray:

sam: on it. can you paste the minimal repro here? i tried the snippet locally and saw the same hang sometimes.

maya: repro below (node):
```
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-small', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }] });
setTimeout(() => stream.cancel(), 10);
await stream.read(); // sometimes never resolves
```

kevin: looks like the docs snippet uses `cancel()` but the runtime guarantees are that `close()` flushes the pending chunks before finishing. i think the example should call `stream.close()` instead and note that cancel is abrupt.

olivia: +1 to kevin. also let's add a one-line note about node versions (v18 vs v20) because the stream impl behaves slightly differently for `setTimeout` granularity. i can push that tiny change.

sam: is `close()` part of the public client API? we should avoid referencing internal methods in docs.

kevin: yes, `close()` is public on the streaming client. it's in the SDK reference (client.stream -> StreamHandle.close()). linking to it from the quickstart would help.

maya: updated the PR: switched to `await stream.close()` and added a parenthetical note + link to the API ref. also liberalized wording from "cancel" -> "stop the stream gracefully".

olivia: left one punctuation nit inline but LGTM otherwise.

sam: looks good to me, will hold until kevin approves so we don't merge without runtime confirmation.

kevin: approved — small change, nice catch. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: merge queued by automerge pipeline (will merge when CI green).

maya: thanks everyone! will monitor if we get any user reports after the deploy.
